picks.what: View of the city, drawing made on Cosimo de’ Medici’s journey
picks.why: true general view with the cathedral towers rising over the town; decorative bands and empty fields trimmed

picks.file: La Catedral de Santiago vista desde La Herradura. Urbano González Varela 1868-1906.jpg
picks.what: The cathedral from La Herradura, painting
picks.why: color view of the cathedral towers above the old town’s roofs

picks.file: Espagne, Santiago de Compostela, Vue prise aussi du nord sur les 2 tours de la façade de la Cathédrale - A10776.jpg
picks.what: The cathedral towers from the north, autochrome (Albert Kahn Museum)
picks.why: early color photo of the two Obradoiro towers and the Azabachería dome; plate label and damaged edges trimmed

gaps: P0, P1: nothing (a 1595 street plan and generic manuscript miniatures); P3: only portraits and a pilgrim watercolor; P6 already covered, panoramas #24 and #25 not better
notes: #15: Commons dates it only ‘before 1906’ (the painter lived 1868–1906), so ‘about 1900’ is an estimate within his working life; if that is too loose, #17 (Mariano Pedrero watercolor, published July 1906) is a firmly dated but weaker fallback — a street view from the Hospital Real with a pilgrim couple in front. #20 (A10775, Azabachería facade and clock tower, 1917) is an alternative autochrome with a stain in the middle. #7 (Obradoiro facade, Vega y Verdugo, 1657) is a landmark drawing passed over for the 1669 general view.
